transcript.text: induction hob keeps turnin off after 5-10 mins on high, have to keep restartin it. drives me nuts. any1 know y?

That usually happens because the hob’s safety system has detected overheating. Induction hobs have internal fans to keep the electronics cool; if those vents are blocked by a cupboard or cluttered with items, the hob will shut down after 5–10 minutes to prevent damage. Please check two things:
1. Are the ventilation slots (usually at the front edge) clear of towels, utensils, or built-in cupboard walls?
2. Are you using induction-compatible pans that are flat and large enough for the zone? If a pan is too small or lifts slightly during cooking, the hob may cut out to protect itself. If both look fine, does an error code (like 'E' followed by a number) appear on the display when it switches off?
vents seem clear, i cant see any. pans are proper induction ones. a code flashes sometimes but too quick to read. started after new drawer unit fitted under it a month ago tho

The fact that this started right after the new drawer unit was fitted is a big clue. Even if the front vents look clear, the new cabinetry might be blocking the air intake or trapping heat around the hob's internal electronics, causing it to shut down as a safety precaution. To help you pinpoint exactly what’s happening (and see if it’s just a blocked vent or a failed fan), I need the make and model number. This is usually on a sticker on the underside of the hob or on your guarantee card; can you find that for me?
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
its a samsung, dont know the model and not going to go looking under it. can u tell me what to do without that?

Yes, I can help without the model number. The timing of the fault (starting after the new drawer unit was fitted) suggests the hob is overheating because airflow is restricted. Even if the front vents look clear, the heat build-up inside the cabinet might be triggering the safety cut-out. Please switch off and isolate the power to the hob. Then check the gap between the bottom of the hob and the top of your new drawer unit. Is there a clear space (at least 2-3cm) for air to flow? If it is tight or touching, that restricted airflow is likely the cause.
not doing that, im not pulling the drawer out or poking about under the hob. is there anything else i can try?

Given that this started immediately after the drawer unit was fitted and the vents look clear from the top, it is likely that the new cabinet is blocking the air intake or trapping heat inside the housing, triggering the safety shut-off. If the airflow restriction is severe enough to cause overheating even with clear front vents, the internal cooling fan may also be struggling or failed. As this involves checking the electrical connections and internal components under the hob, you will need a qualified engineer to inspect it. They can determine if the cabinet needs adjusting for proper ventilation or if the fan needs replacing.

candidates: Overheating protection (blocked vents or failed cooling fan) (high)
Pan compatibility issue (pan too small, wrong material, or lifted during cooking) (medium)
